Clinical Development at BioNova Global Headquarters

BioNova Global Headquarters operates a comprehensive clinical development division dedicated to advancing novel therapeutic agents through rigorous scientific investigation and regulatory compliance. Our clinical programs span multiple therapeutic areas, including oncology, immunology, cardiovascular disease, and rare genetic disorders. Each program is designed to generate robust efficacy and safety data that support regulatory submissions and ultimately benefit patient populations worldwide.

The clinical development process at BioNova Global Headquarters follows a systematic four-phase approach aligned with FDA guidance and international regulatory standards. Phase I trials establish safety profiles, dosage ranges, and pharmacokinetic properties in small healthy volunteer or patient populations. Phase II studies evaluate preliminary efficacy and further characterize safety in target patient populations, typically enrolling 100 to 300 participants. Phase III trials confirm efficacy, monitor adverse reactions, and compare the investigational product to standard treatments or placebo in large randomized controlled populations. Phase IV studies continue safety surveillance following marketing approval.

Quality assurance and data integrity represent fundamental pillars of clinical operations at BioNova Global Headquarters. Our dedicated quality and compliance team implements standard operating procedures that ensure adherence to Good Clinical Practice guidelines, institutional review board requirements, and data protection regulations. Real-time monitoring systems track protocol compliance, adverse event reporting, and data accuracy across all active trials. Regular audits and inspections by internal and external reviewers maintain the highest standards of scientific and ethical conduct.

BioNova Global Headquarters maintains strategic partnerships with leading clinical research organizations, academic medical centers, and contract research entities to execute global trial networks. Our investigators are experienced in enrolling diverse patient populations and managing complex protocols across multiple geographic regions. These collaborative relationships enable efficient patient recruitment, site activation, and data collection while maintaining consistent quality standards and scientific rigor.

The regulatory strategy team at BioNova Global Headquarters works proactively with health authorities including the FDA, EMA, and other national regulatory agencies throughout development. Pre-submission meetings facilitate dialogue regarding trial designs, endpoints, and data requirements before initiating major studies. Post-trial communications ensure efficient review of regulatory submissions and support the probability of approval timelines. Our team maintains expertise in breakthrough therapy designations, accelerated approval pathways, and orphan drug classifications where applicable.

Patient safety monitoring constitutes an essential responsibility throughout all clinical programs at BioNova Global Headquarters.

# Optimizing Bioreactor Scale-Up: Key Considerations for Manufacturing Excellence

Scale-up represents one of the most critical challenges in pharmaceutical manufacturing, and at BioNova Global Headquarters, we've spent considerable time refining our approach to this complex process. When transitioning from laboratory-scale bioreactors to production vessels, engineers must carefully evaluate numerous parameters including agitation rates, oxygen transfer coefficients, and nutrient distribution. The relationship between mixing intensity and cell viability becomes increasingly important as vessel volume increases, and geometric scaling alone often proves insufficient for maintaining consistent culture conditions across larger batches.

One of the most frequently overlooked aspects of bioreactor scale-up involves the fluid dynamics within the vessel itself. As volume increases, the time required for nutrients to distribute uniformly throughout the culture medium can extend significantly, potentially creating micro-environments with variable pH, dissolved oxygen, and osmolality. Our team at BioNova Global Headquarters has observed that implementing advanced computational fluid dynamics simulations during the design phase substantially reduces development timelines and minimizes batch failures during technology transfer.

Temperature control represents another critical variable that demands attention during scale-up operations. Larger bioreactors present increased thermal inertia and reduced surface-area-to-volume ratios, necessitating more sophisticated heat exchange systems and potentially different cooling strategies than those used at smaller scales. We recommend conducting detailed heat transfer analyses and pilot-scale validation studies before committing to production-scale equipment investment.

The integration of real-time monitoring systems has revolutionized how we approach bioreactor control at BioNova Global Headquarters. Modern sensors for dissolved oxygen, pH, viable cell density, and metabolite concentrations provide immediate feedback that enables rapid process adjustments. These tools have proven invaluable for maintaining consistency between batches and ensuring that scaled-up processes perform at least as effectively as their smaller-scale prototypes.

For more technical resources on bioreactor engineering and manufacturing optimization, visit our knowledge portal at bionova.example/engineering. Our team remains committed to advancing pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities and welcomes collaboration with industry partners seeking to optimize their scale-up strategies.

# Optimizing Aseptic Processing: Best Practices for Parenteral Manufacturers

Aseptic processing remains one of the most critical operations in parenteral drug manufacturing, and BioNova Global Headquarters has observed significant advancements in this space over the past several years. The challenge lies in maintaining sterility throughout the entire production chain while simultaneously maximizing efficiency and minimizing product loss. Whether you're manufacturing injectable solutions, suspensions, or lyophilized products, the principles of aseptic technique remain fundamental. Our engineering teams have worked extensively with both traditional isolator systems and newer robotic filling technologies, and the data consistently shows that proper environmental controls and personnel training are the cornerstones of success.

The design of cleanroom facilities has evolved substantially, particularly regarding air handling and particulate control. BioNova Global Headquarters recommends implementing ISO Class 5 environments for critical manufacturing operations, with supporting ISO Class 7 and 8 zones for component preparation and material staging. Isolator systems, in particular, have proven highly effective for high-potency compounds and products requiring enhanced containment. The capital investment in state-of-the-art environmental monitoring equipment has become standard practice, allowing manufacturers to track viable and non-viable particle counts in real-time and make immediate corrections when drift is detected.

Validation of aseptic processes remains a regulatory requirement that demands meticulous attention to detail. Media fill studies, which simulate actual manufacturing operations using sterile growth media instead of drug product, provide crucial evidence of process robustness. BioNova Global Headquarters emphasizes that these studies must encompass worst-case scenarios, including maximum batch sizes, anticipated production speeds, and the most challenging fill weights or volumes. Additionally, environmental monitoring during routine production serves as an ongoing verification tool, helping manufacturers identify trends that might indicate process drift before product quality is compromised.

Personnel training and qualification cannot be overstated when discussing aseptic processing success. BioNova Global Headquarters has implemented comprehensive programs covering gowning procedures, aseptic technique, contamination awareness, and emergency response protocols. Regular competency assessments and contamination control audits ensure that operators maintain their skills throughout their tenure. # Optimizing Tablet Compression Parameters for Enhanced Bioavailability

When developing solid oral dosage forms, tablet compression force represents one of the most critical variables in pharmaceutical manufacturing. At BioNova Global Headquarters, our formulation scientists consistently face the challenge of balancing mechanical strength with dissolution rates. Excessive compression can create tablets that resist disintegration in the gastrointestinal tract, potentially reducing drug bioavailability. Conversely, under-compressed tablets may lack sufficient hardness to survive packaging and transport without degradation. Understanding the relationship between punch force, dwell time, and tablet density is essential for achieving optimal pharmaceutical performance.

The selection of excipients plays an equally important role in compression dynamics. Microcrystalline cellulose, a commonly used binder, exhibits different compression characteristics compared to lactose or mannitol. Our team at BioNova Global Headquarters has documented that varying pre-compression force can significantly influence the final tablet properties, particularly in formulations containing moisture-sensitive active pharmaceutical ingredients. Real-time monitoring of compression parameters using modern instrumented tablet presses provides valuable data for process validation and quality assurance.

Environmental factors within the manufacturing facility also impact compression outcomes. Humidity levels, ambient temperature, and equipment calibration must remain within specified ranges to ensure batch-to-batch consistency. Our engineers have implemented a comprehensive environmental control protocol across all production lines at BioNova Global Headquarters to maintain these critical parameters. Regular preventive maintenance on compression equipment prevents drift in machine performance that could compromise final product quality.

Regulatory compliance adds another layer of complexity to the compression process. The United States Pharmacopeia and European Pharmacopoeia establish specific standards for tablet hardness, friability, and disintegration time. Documentation of compression parameters during manufacturing is essential for FDA submissions and ongoing compliance. BioNova Global Headquarters maintains detailed records of all compression settings and resulting tablet characteristics to support regulatory submissions and demonstrate consistent manufacturing practices.

For more information about our tablet compression protocols and formulation optimization techniques, visit our technical resources at bionova.example/engineering. Our commitment to pharmaceutical excellence ensures that every tablet manufactured meets the highest standards of quality and efficacy.

Scaling Batch Production: Key Considerations for Modern Pharmaceutical Manufacturing

When it comes to ramping up pharmaceutical production, the transition from pilot scale to full manufacturing capacity presents unique engineering challenges. At BioNova Global Headquarters, we've found that successful scaling requires careful attention to equipment selection, process validation, and quality assurance protocols. The fundamental principle remains constant across all batch sizes: maintaining product consistency while optimizing efficiency. However, the practical implementation becomes exponentially more complex as you increase production volume.

One critical area often underestimated during scale-up is heat transfer dynamics. Mixing patterns, temperature uniformity, and reaction kinetics can shift dramatically when moving from a 10-liter vessel to a 500-liter reactor. We've observed instances where reaction times increase unexpectedly due to inadequate agitation in larger tanks, or conversely, where localized heating creates unwanted byproducts. Computational fluid dynamics modeling has become an invaluable tool in our engineering department, allowing us to predict these behaviors before investing in equipment modifications or process adjustments.

Equipment compatibility deserves equally rigorous evaluation during scale-up planning. What works seamlessly with laboratory-grade materials may present unexpected challenges with larger industrial components. Stainless steel specifications, gasket materials, and valve types must all be reconsidered for their performance at increased throughput. Additionally, cleaning validation protocols for larger systems require more extensive documentation and testing to ensure pharmaceutical-grade cleanliness standards are consistently achieved.

Material flow and inventory management become logistically complex at production scale. Raw material staging, in-process storage conditions, and final product hold times all impact shelf-life stability and regulatory compliance. We recommend implementing real-time monitoring systems for temperature, humidity, and pressure during transitions between manufacturing stages. These systems provide the documentation necessary for regulatory submissions while simultaneously allowing operators to identify and address deviations immediately.

For organizations looking to enhance their manufacturing capabilities, detailed process design documentation and risk assessments should precede any equipment procurement. # Advancing Continuous Manufacturing in Pharmaceutical Production

The pharmaceutical industry stands at a pivotal moment as manufacturers increasingly adopt continuous manufacturing processes. At BioNova Global Headquarters, we've observed significant shifts in how companies approach drug production over the past five years. Continuous manufacturing offers distinct advantages over traditional batch processes, including improved product consistency, reduced contamination risk, and substantially lower operational costs. For facilities managing multiple product lines, the flexibility of continuous systems enables faster transitions between compounds while maintaining stringent quality standards.

Implementing continuous manufacturing requires careful consideration of equipment integration and process control systems. Our engineering teams work closely with regulatory consultants to ensure that continuous processes meet FDA expectations for Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and real-time release testing. The investment in automated control systems and advanced sensors provides manufacturers with unprecedented visibility into critical process parameters, allowing for immediate adjustments that maintain product quality throughout production runs.

Scale-up from pilot to commercial continuous manufacturing presents unique challenges that demand rigorous experimental design and validation. BioNova Global Headquarters has developed standardized protocols for residence time optimization, mixing efficiency analysis, and thermal profiling that help minimize development timelines. Companies transitioning to continuous systems often underestimate the importance of thorough hydrodynamic modeling and computational fluid dynamics simulations before commissioning production equipment.

Training and organizational change management often determine success more than the technology itself. Staff accustomed to batch manufacturing mentality require comprehensive education on continuous process monitoring and troubleshooting. BioNova Global Headquarters emphasizes that successful implementation includes documentation strategies, operator competency frameworks, and robust deviation management procedures specific to continuous operations.

For organizations considering this transition, the long-term benefits clearly justify initial capital expenditure and development effort. Understanding HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

If you or a loved one has been diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer, you may feel overwhelmed by new medical terms and treatment options. This information is meant to help you understand what this diagnosis means and what treatments are available.

What Is HER2-Positive Breast Cancer?

Breast cancer starts when cells in the breast grow out of control. HER2-positive means your cancer cells have extra copies of a protein called HER2 on their surface. This protein helps cells grow. When there is too much HER2, the cancer cells may grow faster than other types of breast cancer.

About 1 in 5 people with breast cancer have the HER2-positive type. This type tends to be more aggressive, which means it can grow quickly. However, the good news is that doctors have developed treatments specifically designed to target HER2. These treatments have helped many patients.

Common Symptoms

You may have noticed one or more of these signs:

A lump or thickening in the breast or underarm
Swelling, redness, or warmth in the breast
Pain or tenderness in the breast
Nipple changes, including discharge or turning inward
Skin dimpling or puckering, like an orange peel
A change in breast size or shape

Some people have no symptoms at all. Breast cancer is sometimes found during routine screening mammograms.

How Doctors Diagnose HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

Your doctor starts with a physical exam and imaging tests like mammograms or ultrasounds. If something looks concerning, your doctor will perform a biopsy. A biopsy means taking a small sample of tissue to examine under a microscope.

Lab tests on the tissue sample look for HER2 protein levels. Doctors use two main tests: one called HER2 IHC and another called HER2 FISH. These tests tell your doctor whether your cancer is HER2-positive.

Your doctor may also run other tests to understand your specific cancer better. This information helps create your personal treatment plan.

Treatment Options

Several treatment options are available for HER2-positive breast cancer. Your doctor may recommend one or a combination of these approaches:

Targeted Therapy uses medicines that specifically attack HER2 protein. These drugs stop cancer cells from growing and can help your immune system fight cancer.

Chemotherapy uses strong medicines to kill fast-growing cancer cells throughout your body.

Surgery removes the tumor and possibly surrounding tissue.

Radiation Therapy uses high-energy rays to kill cancer cells.

Hormone Therapy may be used if your cancer also responds to hormones.

Your treatment plan depends on many factors, including how advanced your cancer is, your overall health, and your preferences.

Clinical Trials

Clinical trials test new ways to treat cancer. These studies help doctors learn if new medicines work better or cause fewer side effects than current treatments. One trial being studied is HER2COMBO-201.

Taking part in a clinical trial is voluntary. If you are interested in learning more about available trials, ask your doctor or visit ClinicalTrials.gov.

Remember, a diagnosis of HER2-positive breast cancer is serious, but many treatment options exist. Work with your healthcare team to find the right plan for you.

# Understanding HER2-Positive Breast Cancer and Your Treatment Options

## What Is HER2-Positive Breast Cancer?

Breast cancer develops when cells in the breast grow in an uncontrolled way. HER2-positive breast cancer is a specific type where cancer cells have too much of a protein called HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor 2) on their surface. Think of HER2 like a growth signal on the cancer cells—these extra signals tell the cells to multiply faster than normal cells do.

About 1 in 5 people with breast cancer have the HER2-positive type. The good news is that doctors have developed medicines specifically designed to target HER2, which has improved treatment outcomes for many patients.

## Recognizing Symptoms

You may notice:

- A lump or thickening in the breast or underarm area
- Changes in the size or shape of the breast
- Nipple discharge or inversion (turning inward)
- Skin changes, dimpling, or redness
- Pain or discomfort in the breast area

These symptoms don't always mean cancer—other conditions can cause them too. But if you notice any changes that last more than a few weeks, talk with your doctor right away.

## How Doctors Diagnose HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

Your doctor will likely start with a physical exam and imaging tests like mammography (breast X-rays) or ultrasound. If an area looks concerning, a biopsy may be recommended—this means taking a small tissue sample to examine under a microscope.

The biopsy is crucial because it allows doctors to confirm cancer and test whether the cancer cells have extra HER2 protein. This information helps your medical team create a treatment plan tailored specifically for you.

## Treatment Options Available

Treatment plans are personalized based on factors like the cancer stage, your overall health, and your preferences. Common approaches include:

**Targeted Therapy:** These medicines work like precision tools, targeting the HER2 protein on cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. Your doctor may recommend one targeted therapy or a combination of medicines to attack the cancer in different ways.

**Chemotherapy:** These medicines kill fast-growing cells throughout the body. They're often used alongside targeted therapy.

**Surgery:** Your surgeon may remove the cancer and surrounding tissue.

**Radiation Therapy:** High-energy beams target cancer cells after surgery.

**Hormone Therapy:** Some breast cancers respond to hormonal medicines.

## Clinical Trials: Another Option to Consider

Clinical trials test new or improved ways to treat cancer. These studies help researchers understand whether new treatment combinations work better than standard treatments.

If you're interested in learning more about available trials—such as HER2COMBO-201—ask your medical team. They can discuss whether a trial might be appropriate for your situation. Participating in a trial means you'll receive careful medical monitoring and may have access to new treatment options before they're widely available.

## Moving Forward

Being diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer is challenging, but advances in targeted therapy have transformed this into a condition many people manage successfully. Work closely with your healthcare team, ask questions about your options, and consider reaching out to support groups. You don't have to navigate this alone.

Breast cancer develops when cells in breast tissue grow abnormally and form a tumor. It is one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers worldwide, affecting both women and, rarely, men. Treatment typically involves a combination of surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, and targeted therapies depending on the cancer subtype. HER2-positive breast cancer, for example, responds to specific monoclonal antibody treatments. Clinical trials are testing next-generation targeted therapies and immunotherapies that may offer improved outcomes for patients who have not responded to standard treatments.

Understanding Heart Disease: What You Need to Know

Heart disease affects millions of people, and you're not alone if you or a loved one has been diagnosed with this condition. Understanding what's happening in your body and what your doctor can do to help is an important first step.

What Is Heart Disease?

Heart disease, also called coronary artery disease or ischemic heart disease, happens when the blood vessels that supply your heart become narrowed or blocked. Think of your heart as a muscle that needs a constant supply of oxygen-rich blood to work properly. When fatty deposits build up inside these blood vessels over time, blood flow slows down or gets stuck. This means your heart doesn't get enough oxygen, which can cause serious problems.

Common Risk Factors

Several things can increase your chances of developing heart disease. Some you cannot change, like your age or family history. But many risk factors you can control include smoking, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, being overweight, not exercising enough, eating unhealthy foods, and diabetes. Stress and sleep problems can also play a role. If you have any of these risk factors, talking with your doctor is important.

Recognizing the Symptoms

Heart disease symptoms vary from person to person. Many people experience chest pain or pressure that feels like someone is squeezing their chest. You might feel short of breath, especially during physical activity. Some people feel pain in their arm, neck, jaw, or back. Other signs include fatigue, dizziness, or unusual sweating. Women sometimes have different symptoms, like jaw pain or extreme tiredness. If you ever experience severe chest pain, difficulty breathing, or feel like something is very wrong, call emergency services immediately.

How Doctors Diagnose Heart Disease

Your doctor will start by asking about your symptoms, family history, and risk factors. Blood tests can show if your cholesterol or other markers are unhealthy. An EKG (electrocardiogram) records your heart's electrical activity. Your doctor might use an ultrasound called an echocardiogram to see how your heart pumps blood. Sometimes a stress test shows how your heart responds to exercise. In some cases, your doctor might recommend a cardiac catheterization, where a thin tube is guided to your heart to get a clearer picture.

Treatment Options Available

Treatment depends on how serious your heart disease is. Many people take medications to lower cholesterol, control blood pressure, reduce clotting risk, or ease chest pain. Lifestyle changes like quitting smoking, eating heart-healthy foods, exercising regularly, managing stress, and maintaining a healthy weight make a real difference. Some people need procedures to open blocked vessels or restore blood flow.

Your doctor might also suggest participating in a clinical trial like CARDIO-301, which tests new ways to help people with heart disease. Trials give you access to new treatments while helping doctors learn what works best.

Take Action

If you think you might have heart disease or have risk factors, schedule an appointment with your doctor. Managing heart disease is possible with the right support, treatment, and lifestyle changes. You deserve to feel your best.

Understanding COPD and Your Treatment Options

What Is COPD?

COPD stands for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease. It is a serious lung condition that makes it harder to breathe. If your doctor has told you that you have COPD, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, you are not alone. Millions of people live with this condition every day.

When you have COPD, the airways in your lungs become narrower and damaged over time. This damage makes it difficult for air to move in and out of your lungs. COPD gets worse slowly, which is why it is called chronic, meaning it lasts a long time.

Common Symptoms

If you have COPD, you might notice:

A persistent cough that lasts for weeks or months
Mucus or phlegm when you cough
Shortness of breath, especially when you exercise or move around
Wheezing, which is a whistling sound when you breathe
Chest tightness or pain
Feeling tired more easily than before

These symptoms can make everyday activities like climbing stairs or walking feel exhausting. Many people with COPD feel frustrated or worried about their condition. These feelings are completely normal.

How Doctors Diagnose COPD

If your doctor thinks you might have COPD, they will perform tests. The most common test is called spirometry. During this test, you blow air into a machine that measures how much air your lungs can hold and how fast you can breathe out. This simple test helps your doctor understand how well your lungs are working.

Your doctor may also take a chest X-ray or ask about your medical history and symptoms.

Treatment Options for COPD

There are several ways to manage COPD and feel better:

Inhalers: These are handheld devices that deliver medicine directly to your lungs. Some inhalers help open your airways so you can breathe more easily. Others reduce swelling and mucus in your lungs. Your doctor will show you how to use your inhaler correctly.

Medications: Doctors prescribe different types of medicines depending on how severe your COPD is. Some medicines work quickly when you need them. Others you use every day to prevent symptoms.

Lifestyle changes: Quitting smoking if you currently smoke is one of the most important steps. Exercise, healthy eating, and avoiding lung irritants like pollution can also help.

Pulmonary rehabilitation: This is a program that teaches you breathing techniques and exercises to strengthen your lungs and improve your quality of life.

Oxygen therapy: If your lungs are not getting enough oxygen into your blood, your doctor might recommend supplemental oxygen.

Clinical Trials

Researchers are constantly working to develop new and better treatments for COPD. Clinical trials test new medicines and therapies to see if they are safe and effective. If you are interested in learning about available trials like BREATHE-101, talk with your doctor. They can help you understand whether a trial might be right for you.

Living with COPD takes effort, but with proper treatment and support, many people successfully manage their condition and maintain quality of life.

Understanding Type 2 Diabetes

If you or a loved one has been told you have type 2 diabetes, you're not alone. Millions of people live with this condition every day. We understand that a new diagnosis can feel overwhelming, so we want to help you understand what's happening in your body and what options might be available to you.

What Is Type 2 Diabetes?

Type 2 diabetes is a long-term condition that affects how your body handles blood sugar. Your body normally uses a hormone called insulin to help move sugar from your food into your cells for energy. In type 2 diabetes, your body either doesn't make enough insulin or doesn't use it properly. This is called insulin resistance. When insulin doesn't work the way it should, sugar builds up in your blood instead of getting into your cells.

Type 2 diabetes is sometimes called adult-onset diabetes because it usually develops later in life. However, it can happen at any age.

Common Symptoms

Many people don't notice symptoms at first, which is why regular check-ups are important. When symptoms do appear, they may include:

Feeling very thirsty more than usual
Needing to urinate (pee) more often, especially at night
Feeling more tired than normal
Blurred vision
Cuts or sores that heal slowly
Tingling or numbness in your hands or feet

If you've noticed any of these signs, talking with your doctor is important.

How Doctors Diagnose Type 2 Diabetes

Your doctor can diagnose type 2 diabetes with a simple blood test. The most common test measures your fasting blood sugar, which means your blood sugar level after you haven't eaten for eight hours. Another test called an A1C test shows your average blood sugar over the past three months. Your doctor might also do an oral glucose tolerance test, where you drink a sugary liquid and your blood sugar is checked afterward.

Treatment Options

Managing type 2 diabetes involves several approaches:

Lifestyle changes: Eating healthier foods, exercising regularly, and losing weight can make a big difference.

Medications: Several types of pills and injectable medicines can help your body use insulin better or produce more of it.

Insulin therapy: Some people need insulin injections to help control their blood sugar.

Monitoring: Checking your blood sugar regularly helps you and your doctor know how well your treatment is working.

Clinical Trials: Research Studies for You

If you're interested in exploring new treatment options, clinical trials like DIABPREV-201 may be available. Clinical trials are research studies that test new ways to prevent, detect, or treat health conditions. By participating in a trial, you can access new treatments before they're widely available, and you help advance diabetes care for others.

If you'd like to learn more about whether a clinical trial might be right for you, talk with your doctor or contact BioNova Global Headquarters. We're here to support you on your diabetes journey.

Understanding Type 2 Diabetes

Type 2 diabetes is a condition where your body has trouble managing blood sugar levels. Blood sugar, also called glucose, is fuel that comes from the food you eat. Normally, your pancreas makes a hormone called insulin that acts like a key, helping glucose enter your cells so they can use it for energy. In type 2 diabetes, your body either doesn't make enough insulin or doesn't use it well. This is sometimes called insulin resistance. When insulin doesn't work properly, glucose builds up in your bloodstream instead of entering your cells. Over time, high blood sugar can damage your heart, kidneys, eyes, and nerves.

Type 2 diabetes develops slowly, often over many years. It's the most common type of diabetes, affecting millions of adults. It's sometimes called adult-onset diabetes, though it can happen at any age.

Common Symptoms

Many people don't notice symptoms at first. That's why some people don't know they have it until a blood test shows high blood sugar. When symptoms do appear, they may include:

Increased thirst and frequent urination. You might feel thirsty more often and need to urinate more, especially at night. Unusual fatigue. You may feel tired even when you've rested well. Blurred vision. Your eyesight might become unclear. Cuts or sores that heal slowly. Infections may also happen more often or take longer to heal.

How It's Diagnosed

Your doctor can find type 2 diabetes through simple blood tests. The most common test measures your fasting blood sugar, which is your glucose level after not eating for eight hours. Another test called an A1C shows your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. Your doctor might also do an oral glucose tolerance test, where you drink a sugary liquid and have your blood tested afterward.

Treatment Options

Type 2 diabetes is manageable. Treatment usually starts with lifestyle changes like eating healthier foods, moving your body more, and losing weight if needed. These changes can sometimes bring blood sugar back to normal levels.

If lifestyle changes alone aren't enough, your doctor may prescribe medications. Several types exist, each working differently. Some help your pancreas make more insulin. Others help your body use insulin better. Some slow digestion so glucose enters your bloodstream more slowly. Newer medications can help your kidneys and heart too.

Some people eventually need insulin therapy, where insulin is injected under the skin. This is not a sign of failure. It's simply another tool to manage your condition.

Why Clinical Trials Matter

If you're considering a clinical trial like DIABPREV-201, you're exploring new approaches that might help manage type 2 diabetes better. Research helps doctors find treatments that work for more people. Trials test whether new medications are safe and effective before they become widely available.

If you have type 2 diabetes, talk with your doctor about your options. Whether you choose standard treatment, clinical trials, or both, the goal is the same: keeping your blood sugar in a healthy range and preventing complications. You have choices, and your doctor can help you decide what's right for you.

It affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease, kidney damage, and nerve damage. Management typically includes lifestyle modifications, oral medications such as metformin, and sometimes injectable therapies. Researchers are investigating novel drug classes including dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists that may offer improved blood sugar control with additional metabolic benefits.

Understanding High Blood Pressure and Your Heart Health

If your doctor has told you that you have high blood pressure, you're not alone. Millions of people manage this condition every day. This information is here to help you understand what high blood pressure is and why it matters for your heart health.

What Is High Blood Pressure?

High blood pressure, also called hypertension, happens when the force of blood pushing against your artery walls is too strong. Think of your arteries as tubes carrying blood throughout your body. When pressure builds up inside these tubes over time, it can damage them. This damage can lead to serious heart problems if not managed.

Blood pressure is measured with two numbers. The top number shows pressure when your heart beats. The bottom number shows pressure when your heart rests between beats. Your doctor will tell you if your numbers are too high.

Why Does High Blood Pressure Matter?

When you have high blood pressure for a long time, it makes your heart work harder than it should. This extra work can weaken your heart and damage your blood vessels. Over time, this increases your risk for heart attacks and strokes. That's why managing your blood pressure is so important for protecting your heart.

Common Symptoms

Many people with high blood pressure feel completely fine and have no symptoms. This is actually one reason why high blood pressure can be dangerous—you might not know you have it. However, some people may experience headaches, shortness of breath, or chest discomfort, though these symptoms can have many causes.

How Doctors Diagnose High Blood Pressure

Your doctor measures your blood pressure using a simple device called a blood pressure cuff that wraps around your arm. It doesn't hurt. Your doctor may take your blood pressure several times because a single high reading doesn't always mean you have high blood pressure. If your readings stay high over time, your doctor will likely diagnose you with this condition.

Treatment Options

There are several ways to manage high blood pressure. Your doctor might suggest lifestyle changes first, such as eating a heart-healthy diet, exercising regularly, reducing salt intake, managing stress, and limiting alcohol.

If lifestyle changes aren't enough, many medications can help lower blood pressure. These medicines work in different ways to help your blood vessels relax or help your heart work more efficiently.

Your doctor might also recommend participating in a clinical research trial. Clinical trials test new treatments and help doctors learn better ways to care for patients. The CARDIO-301 trial, for example, is studying new approaches to managing cardiovascular health in people with high blood pressure.

Moving Forward

Managing high blood pressure takes effort, but it's one of the best things you can do for your long-term health. Work closely with your doctor to find the right combination of lifestyle changes and treatments for you. Ask questions and share any concerns you have. Remember, many treatment options are available, and your doctor wants to help you stay healthy.

Understanding Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Your Treatment Options

What is Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

Non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC, is a type of lung cancer that starts in the cells lining the lungs. It is called "non-small cell" because the cancer cells are larger when viewed under a microscope compared to another type of lung cancer. NSCLC is the most common form of lung cancer, accounting for about 8 out of 10 lung cancer diagnoses.

Your lungs are organs that help you breathe. When cancer develops in the lungs, abnormal cells grow and multiply uncontrollably. These cancer cells can spread to other parts of your body over time. Being diagnosed with NSCLC can feel overwhelming, but advances in treatment are giving patients more options and better outcomes than ever before.

Common Symptoms

Many people with early NSCLC may not notice any symptoms. When symptoms do appear, they may include:

A cough that lasts more than a few weeks
Chest pain or discomfort that gets worse when breathing or coughing
Shortness of breath
Hoarseness in your voice
Coughing up blood
Fatigue or weakness
Unexplained weight loss

If you or a loved one has experienced any of these symptoms for more than a few weeks, it is important to talk with your doctor.

How Doctors Diagnose NSCLC

Your doctor may use several tests to diagnose lung cancer:

Imaging tests like CT scans or X-rays show detailed pictures of your lungs
A biopsy, where a small sample of lung tissue is removed and examined under a microscope
Blood tests to look for signs of cancer
Breathing tests to check how well your lungs work

Your doctor may also test your cancer cells to understand what type of NSCLC you have and what mutations, or genetic changes, are present. This information helps guide treatment decisions.

Available Treatment Options

Treatment for NSCLC depends on the stage of your cancer, your overall health, and other personal factors. Common treatment approaches include:

Surgery: Removing the cancerous part of the lung
Chemotherapy: Using strong medicines to kill cancer cells throughout the body
Radiation therapy: Using high-energy beams to target cancer cells
Immunotherapy: Helping your own immune system fight cancer cells
Targeted therapy: Using medicines designed to attack specific mutations in cancer cells

Many patients benefit from combining these approaches. Your doctor will work with you to create a treatment plan that fits your needs.

Clinical Trials and New Options

Clinical trials test new treatment combinations and approaches. Two trials being conducted by BioNova Global Headquarters are ONCORA-301 and ONCORA-101, which are studying immunotherapy and targeted therapy options for NSCLC patients.

Participating in a clinical trial may give you access to newer treatments before they become widely available. Your doctor can discuss whether a clinical trial might be right for you.

Moving Forward

An NSCLC diagnosis is serious, but you are not alone. Talk openly with your healthcare team about your concerns, symptoms, and treatment preferences. Ask questions and take time to understand your options. Support from family, friends, and medical professionals can help you navigate this journey.

Understanding Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Your Treatment Options

What is Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

Non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC, is a type of lung cancer that starts in the cells lining your airways and lungs. It's called "non-small cell" because the cancer cells look larger under a microscope compared to another type of lung cancer. NSCLC is the most common form of lung cancer, accounting for about 8 out of 10 lung cancer cases.

Your lungs are responsible for taking in oxygen when you breathe and releasing carbon dioxide when you exhale. When cancer develops in your lungs, these healthy cells begin to grow in an abnormal, uncontrolled way.

Common Symptoms

You may notice one or more of these signs:

A cough that lasts more than three weeks
Chest pain or discomfort, especially when breathing or coughing
Shortness of breath
Hoarseness or changes in your voice
Coughing up blood
Fatigue or weakness
Recurring lung infections like bronchitis or pneumonia

It's important to know that having these symptoms doesn't mean you definitely have lung cancer. Only your doctor can make that diagnosis. If you've been experiencing any of these symptoms, talk with your healthcare provider.

How NSCLC is Diagnosed

Your doctor will start by asking about your symptoms and medical history. You may undergo several tests:

Imaging tests like chest X-rays or CT scans create detailed pictures of your lungs
A biopsy involves taking a small sample of lung tissue to examine under a microscope
Blood tests provide information about your overall health
Additional tests may help identify specific features of your cancer

These tests help your doctor understand the extent of your cancer and plan the best approach for you.

Understanding Your Treatment Options

Once you're diagnosed, your medical team will discuss treatment possibilities. Two newer approaches show promise for NSCLC:

Immunotherapy uses medicines that help your own immune system recognize and fight cancer cells. Your immune system naturally protects you from harmful invaders, but cancer cells sometimes hide from it. Immunotherapy teaches your immune system to spot and attack these cancer cells more effectively.

Targeted therapy works differently. Your doctor may test your cancer cells for specific genetic changes or mutations—think of these as "mistakes" in the cancer cell's instructions. Targeted therapies are designed to attack cancer cells with these specific mutations while doing less harm to healthy cells. This approach is like using a precision tool rather than a broader approach.

Your doctor will discuss which option might be appropriate based on your specific cancer's characteristics, your overall health, and other factors.

Clinical Trials: Another Path Forward

BioNova Global Headquarters is conducting research studies, including trials like ONCORA-301 and ONCORA-101, that explore new ways to treat NSCLC using immunotherapy and targeted therapy approaches. These trials give eligible patients access to newer treatments while contributing to medical knowledge that may help future patients.

Talking with your healthcare team about whether a clinical trial might be right for you is an important conversation to have. They can explain the potential benefits and risks based on your individual situation.

You're not alone in this journey. Your medical team is here to support you through diagnosis, treatment decisions, and beyond.
clinical_consent_summary_cardio-outcomes:
CARDIO-301 Clinical Trial: What You Need to Know

This summary explains what happens if you join the CARDIO-301 trial. It is not a legal document. Before you decide to participate, you will receive a complete consent form to read and ask questions about.

1. PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The CARDIO-301 trial tests a new medicine called BNV-CRD01. BioNova Therapeutics is studying whether this medicine can help people with heart and blood vessel disease. About 600 people will join this study. The goal is to learn if BNV-CRD01 works better than a placebo (a pill with no active medicine) at reducing heart problems and improving heart health.

2. WHO CAN JOIN

You may be able to join if you:

- Are between 40 and 80 years old
- Have documented coronary artery disease (blockages in the blood vessels that supply your heart) or have an equivalent risk for heart disease
- Have high blood pressure above 140 mmHg, even with stable treatment
- Have high cholesterol (LDL-C above 70 mg/dL)
- Are in good enough overall health to participate (your doctor will assess this)

You cannot join if you:

- Have severe heart failure (NYHA Class IV, meaning your heart is severely weakened)
- Have had a recent stroke
- Have severely reduced kidney function (eGFR below 30)
- Have uncontrolled irregular heartbeat
- Are planning to have a heart procedure within the next 3 months

3. WHAT YOU WILL DO

If you join, you will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. Random assignment means a computer will decide which group you join—not you or your doctor. You have a two in three chance of getting BNV-CRD01 and a one in three chance of getting placebo.

Group 1: BNV-CRD01 10 mg
Group 2: BNV-CRD01 25 mg
Group 3: Placebo (inactive pill)

You will not know which group you are in during the study.

4. HOW LONG IS THE TRIAL

The study duration will be explained in your full consent form. You will have regular visits to the study clinic where researchers will check your health, take blood samples, and ask how you are feeling.

5. POSSIBLE RISKS

Like all medicines, BNV-CRD01 may cause side effects. Possible risks include:

- Mild to moderate side effects such as headache, nausea, or dizziness
- Changes in blood pressure or heart rhythm
- Allergic reactions
- Uncommon but serious risks that we may not know about yet

If you experience severe chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or severe allergic reactions, seek emergency help immediately. You should report all side effects to the study team right away.

If you are in the placebo group, your existing heart condition will not be treated with this new medicine, though you will continue your regular heart medications.

6. POSSIBLE BENEFITS

BNV-CRD01 may help reduce your risk of heart disease. However, we do not yet know if it works. Many people in the placebo group do not experience direct benefits from the study medicine. You may benefit from the extra medical monitoring during the trial.

7. OTHER TREATMENT OPTIONS

You can continue taking your regular heart and blood pressure medicines throughout the study. If you do not join this trial, your doctor can discuss other treatments for your condition.

8. YOUR PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY

Your personal health information will be kept confidential. Only study staff and certain regulatory authorities will see your data. Your information will be stored securely and identified by a study number, not your name. Results will be reported so individuals cannot be identified.

9. YOU CAN QUIT ANYTIME

Joining this trial is completely voluntary. You can stop participating at any time for any reason. Withdrawing will not affect your regular medical care. The study team may also stop your participation if it becomes unsafe to continue.

10. QUESTIONS

Before you sign the consent form, ask the study team any questions you have. You deserve to fully understand what you are agreeing to.

CARDIO-301 Trial: What You Need to Know About Joining

This summary explains what you would be agreeing to if you decide to participate in the CARDIO-301 research study. Please read this carefully and discuss it with your doctor and loved ones before making your decision.

1. What Is This Study About?

The CARDIO-301 study is testing a new medicine called BNV-CRD01 to see if it can help people with heart disease. Heart disease happens when blood vessels that supply your heart become narrowed or blocked, making it harder for your heart to pump blood. We want to learn if this medicine can reduce your risk of future heart problems and help you live a healthier life. The company BioNova Therapeutics is sponsoring this research.

2. Who Can Join?

You may be eligible if you are:
- Between 40 and 80 years old
- Have been diagnosed with coronary artery disease (when the vessels supplying your heart are narrowed) or have serious risk factors for it
- Have a blood pressure reading of 140 or higher even while taking blood pressure medicine
- Have an LDL cholesterol level above 70 mg/dL (this is "bad" cholesterol that can build up in your arteries)
- In generally stable health, able to walk and care for yourself with minimal help

You cannot join if you have advanced heart failure, recently had a stroke, have serious kidney problems, or have irregular heart rhythms that are not controlled.

3. What Will You Do in This Study?

The study involves about 600 people total. You would be randomly assigned, like a coin flip, to receive one of three treatments:
- The lower dose of BNV-CRD01 (10 milligrams)
- The higher dose of BNV-CRD01 (25 milligrams)
- A placebo (a pill with no active medicine)

Neither you nor your doctor will know which treatment you receive. This helps make sure the results are fair and unbiased.

4. What Procedures Will You Undergo?

You will have regular clinic visits to:
- Check your blood pressure and heart rate
- Answer questions about how you are feeling
- Have blood drawn to measure cholesterol and other heart-related markers
- Possibly have heart tests such as an electrocardiogram (a recording of your heart's electrical activity)

These visits will happen more frequently at the start of the study and then less often. The entire study will last several months to a year, though the exact duration will be explained in your full consent form.

5. What Are the Potential Risks?

Like all medicines, BNV-CRD01 could cause side effects. Common side effects in early testing included mild headache, nausea, and upset stomach. Some people experienced dizziness or slight changes in blood pressure. Serious side effects are possible but have been rare so far. There is also a small risk of complications from blood tests or other procedures.

6. What Are the Potential Benefits?

You may benefit if BNV-CRD01 helps lower your cholesterol, reduce your blood pressure, or decrease your risk of a heart attack or stroke. However, there is no guarantee the medicine will help you personally. Even if you receive a placebo, you will get closer monitoring of your heart health.

7. What Other Choices Do You Have?

You can continue with your current heart medicines and care without joining this study. Your doctor can discuss other treatment options available to you.

8. How Will Your Privacy Be Protected?

Your medical information will be kept confidential and stored securely. It will be identified by a study number rather than your name. Only the research team will have access to connect your information to you.

9. Is Participation Voluntary?

Yes. You can join or not join without any penalty. If you join, you can leave at any time without giving a reason. Leaving the study will not affect your regular medical care.

If you have questions, ask the research team before you decide.

BREATHE-101 Clinical Trial Consent Summary

This summary explains what you are agreeing to when you join the BREATHE-101 clinical trial. Please read this carefully. A clinical trial is a research study to test whether a new medicine is safe and works well. This summary is not a legal document. You should also read the full consent form before you decide to participate.

1. Purpose of the Study

The BREATHE-101 trial tests a new medicine called BNV-CPD01. This medicine is being studied to help people with COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). COPD is a long-term lung disease that makes it hard to breathe. The trial will look at whether BNV-CPD01 is safe and how well it works in people like you.

2. How the Trial Works

If you join this trial, you will receive one of three treatments:
- BNV-CPD01 at a low dose
- BNV-CPD01 at a high dose
- A placebo (a pill or injection with no medicine in it)

You will not choose which treatment you get. A computer will randomly assign you to one of these groups. This helps researchers fairly test whether the medicine works better than a placebo.

3. What You Will Do

You will visit the trial clinic several times over the course of the study. At each visit, you may have:
- Blood tests
- Breathing tests
- Chest exams
- Questions about how you are feeling

The trial will last several months. Your study team will tell you the exact schedule at your first visit.

4. Who Can Join

You can join this trial if you:
- Are between 40 and 80 years old
- Have been diagnosed with COPD
- Have an ECOG score of 2 or less (ECOG measures how well you can do daily activities)
- Have lung function (FEV1) between 30% and 70% of what is expected for your age
- Had at least one flare-up of your COPD in the past 12 months
- Currently smoke or used to smoke, with at least 10 pack-years of smoking history (one pack-year means smoking one pack per day for one year)

You cannot join if you:
- Have active asthma or lung cancer
- Use supplemental oxygen at more than 4 liters per minute
- Have had a respiratory infection in the past 4 weeks
- Have had a lung transplant or lung volume reduction surgery

5. Possible Risks

Like all medicines, BNV-CPD01 may cause side effects. We do not yet know all the side effects because this is an early-stage trial. Possible side effects may include nausea, headache, or dizziness. 6. Possible Benefits

BNV-CPD01 may help you breathe better or have fewer COPD flare-ups. However, this medicine is new, and we do not yet know if it will help you personally. You might not benefit at all from taking part in this trial.

You do not have to join this trial. You can continue taking your current COPD medicines. Talk with your doctor about what treatment options are right for you.

We will keep your personal health information private and secure. Your name and medical records will be kept confidential. We will use a code number instead of your name in all trial records.

9. Your Participation Is Voluntary

Joining this trial is completely your choice. You can leave the trial at any time without giving a reason. Leaving the trial will not affect your regular medical care. Your doctor will continue to treat you.

10. Questions and Contact Information

If you have questions about this trial, contact BioNova Global Headquarters. Your study team can answer your questions before you decide to join and at any time during the trial.

Eighty participants will take part in this trial.

You may be eligible to join if you:

- Are between 40 and 80 years old
- Have been diagnosed with COPD
- Are a current or former smoker with at least a 10 pack-year history (for example, smoking one pack per day for 10 years)
- Have experienced at least one COPD flare-up (exacerbation) in the past 12 months
- Have lung function between 30% and 70% of what is expected for your age and size
- Are well enough to participate, with limited activity restrictions

You cannot join if you:

- Also have active asthma or lung cancer
- Use supplemental oxygen at levels above 4 liters per minute
- Have had a respiratory infection in the past 4 weeks
- Have had a lung transplant or lung volume reduction surgery in the past

You will be assigned randomly to one of three groups. Random assignment means the computer decides which group you join—not you or your doctor. The three groups are:

- Low-dose BNV-CPD01

- Placebo (a fake medicine with no active ingredient)

You will not know which group you are in. This helps researchers get fair results.

At each visit, the study team will check your vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature), do blood tests, and test your lung function. You may receive the study medicine through an inhaler or other method your doctor explains. The study team will watch carefully for any side effects and ask you how you are feeling.

Your medical information will be kept confidential. Only the study team and BioNova Therapeutics will see your health records. Your name will not appear in any study reports. However, regulatory agencies may review study records to ensure the research is safe and honest.

Yes. Joining this study is completely voluntary. You can refuse to join or quit at any time without affecting your regular medical care. There is no penalty.

If you have questions, contact your study doctor or the study team before you decide.

STUDY SUMMARY: DIABPREV-201

This summary explains what you need to know before joining the DIABPREV-201 research study. Please read it carefully. This is not a legal document. Before you sign anything, you will receive the full consent form to review with your doctor or study staff.

1. WHAT IS THIS STUDY ABOUT?

This study tests a new medicine called BNV-DX01 to see if it can help people with type 2 diabetes manage their blood sugar better. Type 2 diabetes happens when your body has trouble controlling blood sugar levels. BioNova Therapeutics is sponsoring this research to learn whether BNV-DX01 is safe and effective.

2. WHO CAN JOIN?

You may be able to join if you:
- Are between 30 and 70 years old
- Have been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes
- Have a hemoglobin A1c (a measure of average blood sugar) between 7.0% and 10.5%
- Have a body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 40
- Have been taking metformin (a common diabetes medicine) at the same dose for at least 3 months
- Are generally healthy enough for the study, which means you should be able to do light exercise or be mostly active during the day

You cannot join if you:
- Have type 1 diabetes or gestational diabetes (diabetes during pregnancy)
- Have serious kidney problems (eGFR below 45 mL/min—this is a kidney function measure)
- Have ever had diabetic ketoacidosis (a dangerous blood condition related to diabetes)
- Have used insulin within the past 3 months

3. WHAT WILL HAPPEN IN THIS STUDY?

This is a Phase 2 study, which means researchers are still learning if the medicine works and is safe. About 300 people will join this study. You will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. One group will receive 10 mg of BNV-DX01. Another group will receive 25 mg of BNV-DX01. The third group will receive a placebo, which is a pill with no active medicine. Neither you nor the study staff will know which group you are in.

4. HOW LONG WILL I BE IN THE STUDY?

The study duration will be explained in your full consent form. You will have regular visits where staff will check your blood sugar, take blood samples, and ask about any symptoms you experience.

5. WHAT ARE THE POSSIBLE RISKS?

Like all medicines, BNV-DX01 may cause side effects. The study staff will monitor you carefully. Possible risks include:
- Common side effects that may occur in some people taking this medicine
- Allergic reactions
- Changes in blood sugar levels that could be too high or too low
- Uncommon but serious side effects that will be described in your full consent form

If you experience any concerning symptoms, tell study staff right away. You can leave the study at any time.

6. WHAT ARE THE POSSIBLE BENEFITS?

BNV-DX01 might help you control your blood sugar better. However, there is no guarantee that this medicine will work for you. Some people in the placebo group will not receive the active medicine but will still benefit from close medical monitoring during the study.

7. WHAT ARE OTHER OPTIONS?

Talk with your regular doctor about other medicines and ways to manage type 2 diabetes. You do not have to join this study. Your regular diabetes treatment can continue whether or not you participate.

8. HOW IS MY PRIVACY PROTECTED?

Your medical information will be kept private and secure. Only study staff and regulatory agencies will access your information. Your name will not be used in any reports. Information will be coded with a study number to protect your identity.

9. IS JOINING VOLUNTARY?

Yes. Joining this study is completely your choice. You can leave at any time without any penalty or loss of benefits. Your decision will not affect your regular medical care.

IF YOU HAVE QUESTIONS

Before you decide, ask the study staff any questions you have. You deserve to understand what joining means for you.

DIABPREV-201 Clinical Trial: What You Need to Know Before You Join

This is a plain-language summary of what it means to join the DIABPREV-201 study. This information is not a substitute for the full consent form, which your doctor will review with you. Take time to ask questions before deciding to participate.

1. WHAT IS THIS STUDY ABOUT?

DIABPREV-201 is a research study testing a new medicine called BNV-DX01 to see if it can help people with type 2 diabetes (a condition where your body has trouble controlling blood sugar levels). The study wants to learn if BNV-DX01 is safe and whether it helps lower blood sugar better than a placebo (a pill with no active medicine). About 300 people will take part in this study, and it is being conducted by BioNova Therapeutics.

2. WHAT WILL YOU HAVE TO DO?

If you join, you will receive one of three options: a 10-milligram dose of BNV-DX01, a 25-milligram dose of BNV-DX01, or a placebo. You will not know which one you receive. You will continue taking your regular diabetes medicine (metformin) as you have been.

You will visit the study clinic regularly so doctors can check your blood sugar, measure your weight, and ask how you are feeling. You will need to have blood tests done. The study will last several months, and your doctor will tell you the exact schedule during your first visit.

3. WHO CAN JOIN THIS STUDY?

You can join if you:

Are between 30 and 70 years old
Have type 2 diabetes
Are generally in good health (your doctor will assess this)
Have a hemoglobin A1c (a measure of average blood sugar over three months) between 7.0% and 10.5%
Have a body mass index (BMI, a measure of weight relative to height) between 25 and 40
Have been taking a stable dose of metformin for at least three months

You cannot join if you:

Have type 1 diabetes or gestational diabetes (diabetes during pregnancy)
Have kidney function problems (specifically, an eGFR below 45)
Have had diabetic ketoacidosis (a serious complication where the body produces too many acids)
Have used insulin in the past three months

Your doctor will do tests to make sure you meet these requirements.

4. WHAT ARE THE POSSIBLE RISKS?

Like all medicines, BNV-DX01 may cause side effects. The most common side effects in earlier studies included nausea, headache, and low blood sugar. Some people experienced stomach upset or fatigue (extreme tiredness).

Serious side effects are rare but possible. These include severe allergic reactions, liver problems, or significant drops in blood sugar. Your doctor will monitor you closely and can stop the study medicine if needed.

Because this is a Phase 2 study, we are still learning about this medicine. There may be side effects we have not yet discovered.

5. WHAT ARE THE POSSIBLE BENEFITS?

The main benefit you might experience is better blood sugar control. However, there is no guarantee that BNV-DX01 will help you personally. Even if the medicine works well in this study, you may not benefit. The main reason to join is to help doctors learn whether this new medicine is safe and effective for future patients.

6. WHAT ARE YOUR OTHER OPTIONS?

You do not have to join this study. You can continue taking your current diabetes medicine as prescribed by your doctor. Your doctor can discuss other approved diabetes treatments with you.

7. WILL YOUR INFORMATION BE KEPT PRIVATE?

Yes. Your personal health information will be protected and kept confidential. Your name will not be used in any reports. However, the research team, the study sponsor (BioNova Therapeutics), and regulatory agencies may review your medical records to make sure the study is being conducted safely.

8. CAN YOU STOP PARTICIPATING?

Yes. Joining this study is completely voluntary. You can withdraw at any time without giving a reason, and it will not affect your regular medical care. Your doctor will discuss what happens if you decide to leave early.

If you have questions, ask your doctor or the study team before you decide.

What You Need to Know About the HER2COMBO-201 Trial

This summary explains what you are agreeing to if you join the HER2COMBO-201 research study. This is not a legal document. Before you sign any paperwork, please read this carefully and ask your doctor any questions you have.

1. Why We Are Doing This Study

This study tests a new drug combination to treat HER2-positive breast cancer. HER2-positive means your cancer cells have a protein called HER2 on their surface. We want to see if combining a new medicine called BNV-HER01 with trastuzumab (a drug already used to treat this type of cancer) works better than trastuzumab alone. About 200 people will participate in this study. The study is being run by BioNova Therapeutics.

2. What Will Happen in the Study

If you join, you will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Random assignment means a computer will choose your group by chance. One group will receive BNV-HER01 plus trastuzumab. The other group will receive trastuzumab plus standard care medicines. Standard care means the typical medicines doctors usually prescribe for this condition. You will have an equal chance of being in either group.

You will have regular visits to the clinic for blood work, imaging scans to check your cancer, heart function tests, and physical exams. These visits will help us track how you are doing and watch for any side effects.

3. How Long Is the Study

The study is a Phase 2 trial, which means it is in an early stage of testing. Your active participation could last several months to longer, depending on how you respond to treatment and any side effects you experience. You will need to continue follow-up visits even after your treatment ends.

4. What Are the Possible Risks

Like all medicines, the drugs in this study can cause side effects. Common side effects from these types of medicines may include nausea, tiredness, low blood cell counts, and hair loss. Some side effects can be serious. Because BNV-HER01 is new, we do not yet know all the possible side effects it may cause. Heart problems are a possible risk with these medicines, which is why we will monitor your heart function closely during the study.

5. What Are the Possible Benefits

You may benefit from this treatment. The new drug combination might work better than standard treatment alone. However, we cannot promise that you will personally benefit. The main goal of this study is to gather information that may help future patients.

6. What Are Other Options

You can choose not to join this study. If you do not participate, you can discuss other breast cancer treatment options with your doctor. These options might include different chemotherapy, hormone therapy, or other approved medicines for HER2-positive breast cancer.

7. How Your Privacy Is Protected

Your medical information will be kept private and confidential. Your name and personal details will be replaced with a study number. Only the study team and BioNova Therapeutics will access your information. We may share your medical information with the government health agencies that oversee research safety. We will never sell your information or use it for marketing.

8. Your Participation Is Voluntary

You can join this study or you can refuse. It is completely your choice. If you do join, you can stop participating at any time. Stopping will not affect your regular medical care. Your doctor will continue to treat you even if you withdraw from the study.

You have the right to ask questions at any time before, during, and after the study.

CONSENT SUMMARY: HER2COMBO-201 CLINICAL TRIAL

This is a summary to help you understand what joining the HER2COMBO-201 research study means. Please read it carefully. It is not a legal document, but it will help you know the key facts before you review the full consent form.

1. WHAT IS THIS STUDY ABOUT?

This is a Phase 2 clinical trial run by BioNova Therapeutics to test a new combination treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer. HER2 is a protein found on some cancer cells that helps them grow. You can join if you:
- Are between 18 and 75 years old
- Have been diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer that has spread (we confirm this by looking at tissue under a microscope)
- Have cancer that can be measured on imaging scans
- Have a heart that is pumping well enough (we check this with an echocardiogram, which is an ultrasound of your heart)

You cannot join if you:
- Have an active autoimmune disease (a condition where your immune system attacks your own body)

You will be put randomly into one of two groups. One group gets the new combination: BNV-HER01 plus trastuzumab. The other group gets trastuzumab plus standard care (the usual treatment your doctor would give).

The treatment phase usually lasts several months, but the exact length depends on how well the treatment works for you and whether you experience side effects. You will be followed and monitored even after treatment ends.

Both drugs in this study can cause side effects. Common ones include feeling tired, nausea, hair loss, and low blood cell counts. More serious risks include heart damage, severe allergic reactions, and infections. Because BNV-HER01 is new, some side effects may not be known yet. We will watch you closely and stop treatment if serious problems develop.

6. WHAT ARE THE POSSIBLE BENEFITS?

The study may help control your cancer better than standard treatment alone. However, there is no guarantee that you will benefit. The knowledge gained may help other patients in the future.

You can receive standard treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer without joining this study. Your doctor can discuss these options with you.

Your medical information will be kept confidential and stored securely. Your name and personal details will not be used in any reports. Only the research team and BioNova Therapeutics will have access to your information, plus regulators who oversee the study.

Yes. You can stop participating at any time without penalty or loss of medical care. You do not have to give a reason.

WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT THE ONCORA-101 TRIAL
A Plain Language Summary

This summary explains the main points of the ONCORA-101 research study. It helps you understand what joining this trial means. This is not a legal document. Please read the full consent form before you decide to join.

1. PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

BioNova Therapeutics is testing a new drug called BNV-ONC01. It is designed to treat advanced lung cancer, specifically a type called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Non-small cell lung cancer is the most common type of lung cancer. This drug has not been tested in many patients yet. The main goal of this study is to find the right dose of the drug and learn how safe it is.

2. WHO CAN JOIN THIS STUDY

You may be able to join if you:
- Are between 18 and 80 years old
- Have been diagnosed with advanced lung cancer (stage IIIB or IV) that has been confirmed by a tissue sample
- Have already tried at least one other cancer treatment
- Have healthy enough bone marrow (the tissue inside your bones that makes blood cells)
- Are well enough to do light activities (called ECOG score of 1 or better)

You cannot join if you:
- Have an active autoimmune disease (an illness where your immune system attacks your own body)
- Have an uncontrolled infection
- Have had prior immunotherapy (a type of cancer treatment that uses your immune system)
- Have received bispecific antibody treatment before
- Have cancer that has spread to your brain and is causing symptoms
- Are pregnant or breastfeeding

3. WHAT HAPPENS IN THE STUDY

The study will enroll about 60 people total. You will receive BNV-ONC01 as an injection or infusion (medicine given through your vein). The study uses a dose escalation design. This means the first group of people gets a lower dose. If it is safe, the next group gets a slightly higher dose. This continues until researchers find the best dose.

You will have regular visits to the clinic. These visits will include blood tests, imaging scans (like CT scans), and physical exams. These tests help doctors check how you are responding to the drug and monitor for side effects.

4. HOW LONG IS THE STUDY

The study continues until the drug stops working or side effects become too serious. Most participants stay in the study for several months to over a year. After the study ends, researchers will continue to follow your health for a period of time.

5. POSSIBLE RISKS

Like all drugs, BNV-ONC01 can cause side effects. We do not yet know all the risks because this is an early-stage trial. Possible side effects may include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, low blood cell counts, and infections. Some people may have serious side effects. In rare cases, new drugs can cause life-threatening reactions. The dose escalation design means people in early groups get lower doses with potentially fewer side effects, but we cannot guarantee safety.

6. POSSIBLE BENEFITS

The drug may help slow or stop your cancer growth. Some people may see their tumors shrink. However, there is no guarantee the drug will help you personally. You will receive close medical monitoring and extra clinical care during the study.

7. OTHER TREATMENT OPTIONS

If you do not join this study, you can discuss other cancer treatments with your doctor. These may include chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or other clinical trials.

8. YOUR PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY

Your medical information will be kept private and protected. Your identity will be coded with a number in study records. Only the study team will know your name. Your information may be reviewed by regulatory agencies and BioNova Therapeutics. Your privacy will be protected by law.

9. YOU CAN CHOOSE TO PARTICIPATE

Joining this study is completely voluntary. You can say no, and your regular medical care will not be affected. If you join, you can quit at any time for any reason. Your doctor will continue to care for you.

If you have questions, ask the study team before you decide.

- Blood tests and imaging scans to check your health and measure your tumors
- Physical exams
- Recording of any side effects you experience

4. HOW LONG IS THE TRIAL

The trial lasts as long as your cancer responds to treatment or until you choose to stop. Some participants may stay in the trial for many months or longer.

5. POSSIBLE BENEFITS

The new mAb may help slow your cancer growth or shrink your tumors. Some people may live longer because of this treatment. However, the treatment may not work for you. This trial is designed to help future patients, but it may or may not help you directly.

6. POSSIBLE RISKS

Like all cancer treatments, the mAb may cause side effects. Common side effects include fatigue (extreme tiredness), nausea, vomiting, and rash. Because this is a new treatment, some side effects may not be known yet. Serious side effects are possible, including immune system problems. You will be told about any new risks discovered during the trial.

If you receive a placebo, you will only get standard care, which may be less effective than adding the new mAb.

7. OTHER TREATMENT OPTIONS

Talk with your doctor about other cancer treatments available to you outside of this trial. Your doctor can explain other options and help you decide what is best for your situation.

8. YOUR PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY

Your medical information will be kept private and secure. BioNova Therapeutics will use your information only for this trial. Your name will not appear in any reports.

9. YOUR CHOICE TO PARTICIPATE

Joining this trial is completely voluntary. You can choose to join or not join. If you join, you can leave the trial at any time without penalty. Your regular medical care will not be affected if you decide not to participate or if you leave the trial early.

If you have questions, please ask your study doctor before you decide.
